brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.evidence: 7 full pieces at level 0: center (0,0) plus its six neighbours (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,-1), (0,1), (1,-1), (1,0).
7 top covers, one on each piece (cover:*;full;top).

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: 18 caps, one on every open outer edge the configurator offered (3 per ring cell × 6). No offered cap socket is left empty.
6 joint bolts join the center to each ring cell, which fixed the LOOSE_BODY warning. check_build: no issues, meshClash clear.

finish.summary: I built a seven-cell honeycomb with 7 full pieces in a flower pattern. It has 7 top covers, 18 caps on every open outside edge, and 6 joint bolts to hold it together. The final check found no issues and no part collisions. This confirms the parts fit, not how much weight it can hold.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
